AND AWARD DATED: 27/10/2018,
PASSED IN MVC NO.6948/2017,

ON THE FILE OF THE XXI ADDITIONAL SMALL CAUSES JUDGE & XIX ACMM., MEMBER,
MACT, BENGALURU (SCCH-23), PARTLY ALLOWING THE CLAIM PETITION FOR COMPENSATION AND SEEKING ENHANCEMENT OF COMPENSATION.
 THIS APPEAL, COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
THE COURT DELIVERED THE FOLLOWING:
 JUDGMENT 1.

The claimant, being dissatisfied with the compensation of Rs.3,73,519/- awarded by the Tribunal,
is in appeal.
2. The fact that the accident occurred and the further fact that the offending vehicle was insured is not in dispute.
3. It is not in dispute that the insurer is liable to pay the compensation as the offending vehicle was insured.

4. The Tribunal, on assessment of the evidence, has recorded a finding that the claimant has suffered the following injuries :
i. Segmental fracture of both bones of left leg.
ii. Contusion left iliac region.
iii. Underwent interlock nailing of left tibia.

5. The Tribunal has thereafter awarded the following sums as compensation :
 Sl. Amount  Particulars  No. in (Rs.)
 1. Pain and sufferings 40,000/-

2 . Loss of future earnings 2,26,800/-
 3.

Medical expenses 61,719/-
 4. Conveyance, nourishment and 30,000/-
 nutritious food

Future medical expenses 15,000/-
 Total 3,73,519/-
6. The Doctor, who was examined, stated that the claimant had suffered 66% disability to the limb and 22% disability to the whole body.
However, the Tribunal, on an analysis of the medical evidence, has concluded that the claimant has suffered permanent disability to the extent of 15% to the whole body.

In my view, since the treated Doctor had stated that the claimant had suffered disability to the extent of 22% to the whole body, it would be appropriate to hold that the claimant had disability to the extent of 22% to the whole body.
7. The Tribunal has determined the monthly income, notionally at Rs.9,000/-.

Since there is no credible documentary evidence to ascertain the actual monthly income, it would be appropriate and prudent to adopt the monthly income determined by Karnataka State Legal Services Authority,
which, for the accident of the year 2017, would be Rs.11,000/-.

8. As the claimant has suffered disability to the extent of 22%, 25% of the monthly income is required to be added towards future prospects which would result in the monthly income of Rs.13,750/- [Rs.11,000/- + (Rs.11,000/- x 25/100)].
9.
The claimant was aged 44 years, and hence, the multiplier of '14' would have to be applied and

Consequently, the claimant would be entitled to a sum of Rs.5,08,200/- (Rs.13750/- x 12 x 14 x 22%) towards 'loss of future income'.
10.
The Tribunal has awarded a sum of Rs.40,000/- towards 'pain and sufferings'.

In my view, the claimant has suffered 66% disability to the limb and it would be appropriate to award Rs.75,000/-
towards 'pain and sufferings'.
11. The Tribunal has not awarded any sum towards 'loss of amenities'.
Having regard to the fact that claimant has suffered 22% disability to the whole body, it would be appropriate to award Rs.75,000/- towards 'loss of amenities'.

12. A sum of Rs.61,719/- awarded towards 'medical expenses', Rs.15,000/- towards 'future medical expenses' and Rs.30,000/- towards 'conveyance, nourishment and nutritious food' are just and proper and are accordingly affirmed.

13. Consequently, the claimant is entitled to the following sums :

Thus, the claimant is held entitled to the total compensation of Rs.7,64,919/- as against Rs.3,73,519/-, along with interest at the rate of 6% per annum from the date of petition till its realization.
15. The Insurance Company is directed to deposit the amount of compensation awarded within two months from the date of receipt of a certified copy of this judgment.
16. The disbursement of the amount shall be in terms of the Award of the Tribunal.
The appeal is accordingly allowed in part.
